cases.translation: Everyone keeps saying: the Kremlin, the Kremlin.
cases.explain: In direct speech the word is simply being named, so it stands in the dictionary form — the nominative.

cases.sentence: Сам я ни разу не видел ___.
cases.translation: I myself have never once seen the Kremlin.
cases.explain: The object of a negated transitive verb («не видел») regularly takes the genitive, so Кремль becomes Кремля.

cases.sentence: Проходил по ___ с севера на юг.
cases.translation: I walked across Moscow from north to south.
cases.explain: The preposition «по» in the sense of movement around or across a place governs the dative: по Москве.

cases.translation: To start with, I drank a glass of zubrovka.
cases.explain: After a container or measure word («стакан») the substance measured goes into the genitive: стакан зубровки.

cases.sentence: Я вышел на ___, когда уже рассвело.
cases.translation: I stepped out into the open air when it was already light.
cases.explain: «На» with motion towards something takes the accusative; воздух is inanimate, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.translation: I woke up in the morning in someone's unknown entrance hall.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location, not direction) requires the prepositional case: в подъезде.

cases.sentence: Он уснул на ступеньке с ___ у сердца.
cases.translation: He fell asleep on the step with the little suitcase against his heart.
cases.explain: «С» meaning 'together with' governs the instrumental, so чемоданчик becomes чемоданчиком.

reading.question: What does everyone talk about that the narrator himself has never seen?
reading.explain: The chapter opens with everyone talking about the Kremlin, which Venichka has never once managed to see.

reading.question: What is the first thing Venichka drinks after getting off at Savyolovsky station?
reading.explain: He says he starts with a glass of zubrovka, calling it the best morning remedy people have devised.

reading.question: What did Venichka's acquaintance claim about coriander vodka?
options: That it acts on a person inhumanely
That it is the best morning drink
That it is impossible to find
That it puts you straight to sleep
reading.correct: That it acts on a person inhumanely
reading.explain: The acquaintance's claim is that coriander vodka strengthens the limbs while weakening the soul — acting inhumanely.

reading.question: How did the coriander vodka affect Venichka compared with that description?
options: The opposite: his soul grew stronger and his limbs weakened
It had no effect at all
reading.correct: The opposite: his soul grew stronger and his limbs weakened
reading.explain: He reports the reverse effect, and adds that this is no less inhumane.

reading.ru: На улице Чехова я выпил два стакана охотничьей.
reading.question: What does Venichka distinctly remember drinking on Chekhov Street?
reading.explain: This is the one stretch of the evening he says he remembers clearly.

reading.ru: Когда я ищу Кремль, я неизменно попадаю на Курский вокзал.
reading.question: What always happens when Venichka goes looking for the Kremlin?
options: He ends up at the Kursk railway station
He falls asleep on the way
He turns round and goes home
reading.correct: He ends up at the Kursk railway station
reading.explain: The running joke of the chapter is that searching for the Kremlin always lands him at the Kursk station instead.

reading.ru: Проснулся утром в чьём-то неведомом подъезде.
reading.question: Where does Venichka wake up at the start of the day?
options: On a bench at the station
reading.explain: He fell asleep on the fortieth step of an unknown entrance hall and woke there in the morning.

reading.ru: Я выпил ещё на шесть рублей.
reading.question: What calculation has just upset Venichka?
options: That he drank another six roubles' worth and cannot recall what
That he slept for six hours
reading.correct: That he drank another six roubles' worth and cannot recall what
reading.explain: What grieves him is not the money but that nobody will ever know what he drank, or in what order.

reading.ru: Всё на свете должно происходить медленно и неправильно.
reading.question: What principle does Venichka state about how things in the world should happen?
options: Slowly and wrongly, so that a person cannot grow proud
reading.correct: Slowly and wrongly, so that a person cannot grow proud
reading.explain: He offers this as consolation for not knowing where he is: things must go slowly and wrongly so a person stays sad and bewildered.

reading.ru: Время от рассвета до открытия магазинов.
reading.question: Which stretch of time does Venichka call the most powerless and shameful in his people's life?
options: From dawn until the shops open
reading.correct: From dawn until the shops open
reading.explain: The chapter ends with this lament about the hours before the shops open.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Venichka has heard about the Kremlin from everyone but has never seen it himself?
sentences: Ото всех я слышал про него, а сам ни разу не видел.
Сколько раз уже (тысячу раз), напившись или с похмелюги, проходил по Москве с севера на юг, с запада на восток, из конца в конец, насквозь и как попало – и ни разу не видел Кремля.
highlight.explain: The second sentence contrasts what he has heard from everyone with what he has actually seen.

highlight.question: Which sentence reports what Venichka's acquaintance said coriander vodka does to a person?
sentences: А потом – на Каляевской – другой стакан, только уже не зубровки, а кориандровой.
Один мой знакомый говорил, что кориандровая действует на человека антигуманно, то есть, укрепляя все члены, ослабляет душу.
Со мной почему-то случилось наоборот, то есть душа в высшей степени окрепла, а члены ослабели, но я согласен, что и это антигуманно.
Поэтому там же, на Каляевской, я добавил еще две кружки жигулевского пива и из горлышка альб-де-дессерт.
highlight.explain: The acquaintance's claim — strengthening the limbs while weakening the soul — is the fourth sentence.

highlight.question: Which sentence states the rule that whenever he goes looking for the Kremlin he ends up at the Kursk station?
sentences: А потом я пошел в центр, потому что это у меня всегда так: когда я ищу Кремль, я неизменно попадаю на Курский вокзал.

Мне ведь, собственно, и надо было идти на Курский вокзал, а не в центр, а я все-таки пошел в центр, чтобы на Кремль хоть раз посмотреть: все равно ведь, думаю, никакого Кремля я не увижу, а попаду прямо на Курский вокзал.
highlight.explain: The first sentence states the rule; the second only describes what he did yesterday.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives the real reason Venichka feels aggrieved?
sentences: Обидно мне теперь почти до слез.
Не потому, конечно, обидно, что к Курскому вокзалу я так вчера и не вышел.
Обидно вот почему: я только что подсчитал, что с улицы Чехова и до этого подъезда я выпил еще на шесть рублей – а что и где я пил?
Никто этого не знает, и никогда теперь не узнает.
highlight.explain: He rules out two reasons before naming the real one: six roubles' worth of drink he cannot account for.
